clue.text: Childminder, diminutive model

parts.note: baby used as an adjective means tiny, as in a baby carrot
an artist's model is a sitter

explanation.surface: A nanny who is also a petite fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone paid to look after children while the parents are out is a minder of children in the plainest sense.

clue.text: Haircuts, one shilling and sixpence originally

parts.note: bob was old British slang for a shilling coin

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word sixpence, keeping only its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of sixpence

explanation.surface: An old-money price list for haircuts: one and six a time.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money had shillings and pence; a bob was a shilling, and 'one and six' meant one shilling and sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: Short hairstyles cut level around the head are called bobs, so the plural names styles of cut.

clue.text: Spicy dish with added port

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a metal bowl
more is something added, an extra

explanation.surface: A curry served with a glass of port alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine to go with the dish, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore in Maryland is a major American seaport city on Chesapeake Bay.

clue.text: This may help one to make progress in street (Essex town street) on one

definitions.text: This may help one to make progress

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street
Epping is a market town in Essex, north-east of London
ST is the usual abbreviation for street again
on means placed after, followed by the word one itself

explanation.surface: Getting ahead by walking along a street in an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed words are the wordplay itself, and 'on one' simply means followed by ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone is literally a stone for crossing water, and figuratively any stage that helps someone advance towards a goal.

clue.text: Head in charge suggests subject

parts.note: the top is the head of something
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A headteacher in charge proposes what the class will study.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the theme or matter under discussion, so it is a synonym of subject in that sense.

clue.text: Clear former partner, one on a charge

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
taken as written
a rate is a charge, as in an hourly rate

explanation.surface: Acquitting an ex-partner who has been charged with a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a criminal charge, which fits 'clear', but here it is a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to free them from blame or accusation, which is clearing their name.

clue.text: Painter, Lowry, ultimately shown in part of India

indicators.note: something shown in a place is displayed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the artist's name is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of Lowry

explanation.surface: An exhibition of one painter, Lowry, being held in India.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of industrial scenes, which makes him look like the answer, but only his last letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Carrying far too much weight to be self-assured in part

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the following words is needed, a run of letters within them

parts.note: runs from the end of to through be into the start of self

explanation.surface: Overweight but trying to stay confident about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes a person so overweight it endangers health, far beyond merely carrying a few extra pounds.

clue.text: Waving at us at road leading to expressway

indicators.note: waving is moving back and forth, so the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters, ten in all

explanation.surface: Someone waving at drivers from a slip road onto a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An autostrada is an Italian motorway, a fast multi-lane highway of the kind called an expressway.

clue.text: A measure of protection in case of fire?

definitions.text: A measure of protection in case of fire?

parts.words: A measure of protection in case of fire?
parts.note: surface reading: a safety precaution against flames, like an extinguisher or alarm
setter's reading: gunfire, and a garment worn to stop shots

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' reads as flames in a building; the question mark signals it means being fired at with guns.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment protects a wearer's torso from gunshots, so it is a safeguard against being shot at.

clue.text: Leading actress left in embrace of boyfriend from French town

parts.note: Joan Fontaine was a Hollywood leading lady, Oscar-winner for Suspicion

indicators.note: being in someone's embrace means being held inside their arms, so one letter is wrapped by another word

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A star actress who has left her boyfriend's arms, the man coming from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Fontainebleau is a town south-east of Paris famous for its royal château and forest.

clue.text: Ineffective type, Women's Institute representative

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A feeble delegate sent by the local Women's Institute.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a weak, timid person who lacks the courage or force to get anything done.

clue.text: Chars set about scrubbing, initially with detergents

indicators.note: to be set about something is to be placed around it, so the first word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is an old British word for a cleaning lady

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter of scrubbing is used

parts.note: the first letter of scrubbing

explanation.surface: Cleaning ladies getting to work scrubbing with their soap powders.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergents are chemical agents used for washing, and cleansers is a general word for such cleaning products.

clue.text: A US writer pens short ballad making a prophetic disclosure

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so the writer's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of tales and poems

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the song loses its final letter

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean narrative song

explanation.surface: An American author writing a brief song that foretells doom.
explanation.definitionFit: Apocalypse comes from Greek for uncovering or revelation, the name of the biblical book prophesying the end of the world.

clue.text: I hope Inca flourished in ancient land

indicators.note: to flourish something is to wave it about with a flamboyant gesture, so the letters are flung into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters, nine in all

explanation.surface: Wishing that an Inca prospered in some long-gone kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourished' reads as thrived, which suits an Inca empire; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was an ancient seafaring civilisation on the coast of what is now Lebanon and Syria.

clue.text: One who cheats a fair deal?

definitions.text: One who cheats a fair deal?

parts.words: One who cheats a fair deal?
parts.note: surface reading: someone who swindles a person out of an honest bargain
setter's reading: a deal of the pack at the card table, rigged by a skilled cheat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' sounds like a business bargain, but the question mark points to dealing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a professional gambler who wins by cheating at card games, often by dealing dishonestly.

clue.text: Colour included in 'Chambers'

indicators.note: included in says the word sits within the quoted one, contained among its letters

parts.note: found inside the dictionary's name, after the first two letters

explanation.surface: A colour word that appears in the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary most British crossword setters use.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the yellowish-orange colour of fossil resin, also the middle traffic light.

clue.text: Oil in two colours

wordplay.note: two colour names placed side by side

explanation.surface: An oil painting done in just two colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' suggests oil paint, but it is crude petroleum.
explanation.definitionFit: Black gold is a popular nickname for crude petroleum, because it is dark and immensely valuable.

clue.text: Caught famous pianist in musical

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Dame Myra Hess was a celebrated British concert pianist

explanation.surface: A famous pianist found playing in a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the 1980s stage show with music by Benny and Björn of ABBA, set around a world championship match.

clue.text: Flying her, I nearly, at first, touch down in German region

indicators.note: flying suggests letters tossed through the air and landing in a different order

parts.note: the fodder letters

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of nearly is taken

parts.note: the first letter of nearly
to touch down is to land an aircraft

explanation.surface: A pilot nearly landing her plane somewhere in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rheinland, or Rhineland, is the area of western Germany along the River Rhine.

clue.text: Crayfish in sea? No glut, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters end up out of order

parts.note: the fodder letters, nine in all

explanation.surface: A fisherman laments that crayfish are scarce in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Langouste is the French name for the spiny lobster, often called crayfish or crawfish in English.

clue.text: The French writer turned up somewhere in Asia

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, the opposite direction

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A French author who showed up somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is the Himalayan country between India and China, home of Everest.

clue.text: Section of gate at entrance is corroded

indicators.note: a section of the words is a slice taken from them, letters lying across the boundaries

parts.note: from the end of gate, through at, into the start of entrance

explanation.surface: Rust has corroded part of the gate at the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that is corroded has been gradually eaten away by rust or chemical attack.

clue.text: Cook from Derbyshire town, not well

indicators.note: not well instructs dropping the word well from the town's name

parts.note: Bakewell is a market town in Derbyshire, famous for its tart and pudding

explanation.surface: A cook from Derbyshire who has been feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not well' reads as sick but tells you to remove WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To bake is to cook food by dry heat in an oven, so it is a specific method of cooking.

clue.text: Can move around

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for prison, as is the other word
second meaning: to mix by moving a spoon around

explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb meaning be able; it is the noun, slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old slang for a prison, like can, and as a verb means to agitate or mix a liquid.

clue.text: Beaten in the last stride? That stopped Pipe getting carried away

definitions.meaning: first meaning: narrowly losing a race at the very end

definitions.text: That stopped Pipe getting carried away
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: what foils racehorse trainer Martin Pipe's runner just short of the winning line

explanation.walkthrough: Martin Pipe was a champion British racehorse trainer; the second sentence imagines his runner caught right at the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means narrowly defeated at the very last moment, like a horse overtaken just before the finishing line.

clue.text: Cockney lists fish?

indicators.note: Cockney speakers famously drop their aitches, so the initial letter goes

parts.note: a ship that lists heels over to one side

explanation.surface: A London street trader writing out a list of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which omits the h sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish, a traditional Cockney food served jellied.

clue.text: Move in game on horseback, by duke down by one

parts.note: a jockey who is riding is said to be up
by can join two things, like and
under means below or down
surface padding: this word cannot be fitted into the wordplay

explanation.surface: A riding duke dismounting during a game of polo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' and 'by one' are hard to account for; the clue seems loosely built from UP, AND and UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An up-and-under is a rugby tactic: a high kick that lets chasing players arrive as the ball comes down.
